page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring a constrained vCPU profile designed for memory-intensive workloads that require lower compute core counts. Powered by a 3.525 GHz AMD EPYC 7763 processor using the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 4 dedicated virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 512 KB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, with hardware support for AES, VAES, SHA extensions, AVX, and AMD SVM virtualization.

The instance delivers 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Storage capabilities include a bundled 322 GB local SSD for temporary scratch space and paging, alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage remote disks. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs configured on this instance type.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, recording a stress-ng single-core score in the upper quartile (2702.28) and a Geekbench single-core result of 1592.0. However, multi-core metrics reflect the restricted 4-vCPU hardware allocation, showing weaker aggregate throughput with a multi-core stress-ng result of 5399.28 and Geekbench multi-core score of 3646.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 258.23 GB/sec in small cached reads, tapering to 39.33 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads and 22.83 GB/sec on large block writes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the constrained core design allows organizations to reduce per-core software licensing expenses while retaining access to the full 64 GB memory footprint and local NVMe-class SSD storage of an 8-vCPU chassis. The hardware profile is best aligned with in-memory caching systems, moderately threaded relational databases, analytics data stores, and backend enterprise services needing significant RAM without substantial parallel compute requirements.

A 322 GB local SSD is included for high-speed temporary storage, while GPU acceleration is omitted. Performance testing shows solid single-thread execution, highlighted by a strong stress-ng single-core score of 2702.28, though multi-threaded scores remain modest due to the 4-thread hardware boundary.
